prompt: Talk trash on behalf of the U.S. Navy about the Battle of Midway. Four carriers in five minutes. Rub it in.
response:
Alright, buckle up.

Four carriers. FOUR. In basically an afternoon. Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, Hiryu—the same proud flattops that hit Pearl Harbor six months earlier—all sent straight to the bottom of the Pacific. You brought your best carrier fleet in the world to Midway, and we handed you a filing cabinet full of death certificates.

You wanna talk about timing? Our dive bombers showed up while your decks were stacked with fueled planes and loose bombs. Absolute worst possible moment for you. Fuel lines everywhere, ordnance not stowed—it was a floating fireworks factory, and we brought the match. Enjoy the fireworks show, courtesy of the SBD Dauntless.

Oh, and we KNEW you were coming. Broke your codes. You thought "AF" was a secret? We had you scheduled on our calendar. We RSVP'd to your ambush and flipped it into yours. You planned the perfect trap and walked face-first into ours.

You lost four carriers. We lost one—the Yorktown—which, fun fact, you thought you'd already sunk at Coral Sea. Surprise! We patched her up in 72 hours and sailed her right back into the fight. That's the difference between us: you lose a carrier, it's a national tragedy. We lose one, we tape it back together over the weekend.

And the pilots. Your irreplaceable aviators, your veteran mechanics, all the way to the bottom. That's the part that really stung, isn't it? You never rebuilt that talent. Midway didn't just cost you steel—it cost you the initiative for the entire rest of the war.

June 4th, 1942. The day the Pacific tide turned. From that morning on, it was all downhill for you and all uphill for us.

Four carriers. Five minutes. Frame it and hang it on the wall.

Go Navy. 🇺🇸⚓
